expected: Atlas is the default landing view; live map or vector fallback preserves state selection. The map remains a full-width interactive canvas before, during and after selecting a state; the inspector opens without shrinking the map. The rail uses real manager, visit and trip records and opens the command center. Selecting Florida shows contextual actions that open real existing workflows and preserve the state context. Field intelligence is optional and the main map remains prominent. Field week displays saved future visits without invented records. Map selection keeps a single wide canvas; the rail offers a real next-action shortcut from saved records. The geographic visit intensity and totals reflect the selected date window without inventing visits. Census ZIP area results appear with coordinates, source year and transparent distance limitations.

expected: Mobile People switch remains visible, and all other field tools preserve their existing navigation and data. Each shortcut opens the corresponding existing working tool and supports returning to Atlas. Mission Control and saved-record search are available without leaving the shared workspace. Available Census places and saved ZIP assignments appear with clear source scope, and selecting them opens territory explorer. Mission Intelligence suggests a grounded field circuit, its reasons are visible, and the click carries real managers and dates into the existing trip builder without creating a booking. The regional visualization uses only saved team data, supports three measures, and navigates into a selected state. Existing pages are reachable directly through search, without creating replacement tool screens. Each context action opens an existing relevant screen or permitted record and never assumes external calendar data. Destination Weather Intelligence returns genuine NWS seven-day forecasts when available, displays weather cues and source dates, and never implies flight-delay certainty. Flight DNA shows separate historical, current FAA/NOAA observations and seven-day NWS trip-date conditions; future weather cues are not treated as observed flight operations. The national ZCTA index uses only official Census geographic records, and on source failures returns unavailable status rather than a fabricated ZIP location. Numeric global searches show authoritative published Census ZCTA matches and route directly into the regional ZIP tool. Backup v2 includes trainer availability; legacy v1 restores with a limitation warning; impossible dates return validation errors. Data view displays real integrity reports and explicit evidence-based source probe results; no invented reliability claims. Every CSV manager+assignment row commits atomically; app foreground and WebSocket reconnection reconcile missed team changes. Daily and user-triggered public source probes persist a timestamped snapshot; failed checks never appear as green availability. Separately revocable trainer links work without sign-in, owner permissions control invitations, and the bound seat cannot be impersonated by a URL trainerId. Invalid or duplicate geographic assignments and itinerary changes cannot silently corrupt the shared schedule. Workspaces provision atomically; multi-editor backups restore without granting historical invitations access. Realtime messages are sent only to connections whose underlying trainer link is still valid and assigned to the matching workspace.

expected: No horizontal overflow; controls, sheets, and tabs remain reachable at narrow widths and in both themes. The logo returns to Atlas; available counties open the relevant territory explorer; stale success notices do not follow unrelated navigation. The three intelligence cards are touch reachable and the command page retains mobile navigation. The map has a readable segmented lens control, larger tap areas and a consistent Miami Vice identity in both themes. Mobile Travel shows the next real booked flight on this device or the next shared saved trip, opening the existing Booked Flights or Trips tools. Mobile Mission Intelligence stays readable and all action controls remain reachable without horizontal page overflow. Every Travel tool remains discoverable through a readable, horizontally scrollable tab row; no hidden controls. Shared typography, navigation controls and cards remain legible and consistent across both themes and phone sizes. The contextual bar is visible above the content, stays within phone width, and does not cover the bottom navigation. The weather strip is swipeable, the travel day is highlighted when published, and unsupported point forecasts display a clear unavailable message.
